fields.name: Anton Ryzhikov
fields.title: Engineering Manager
fields.whoAmI: Anton Ryzhikov is an Engineering Leader with over a decade of experience building and scaling high-impact software products across global organizations. He has successfully led cross-functional engineering teams of up to 18 members, driving technical vision, architectural evolution, and operational excellence in fast-paced environments. Anton excels at transforming complex technical challenges into scalable solutions — from architecture migrations and launching kiosk serving millions of monthly orders, to establishing sustainable engineering practices like feature ownership, ADRs, and incident management. He has been accountable for systems handling up to 40% of company revenue. His leadership style emphasizes trust, team autonomy and outcome-driven delivery.

workEntries.description:
- Led sub-teams of up to 18 members overall, responsible for Point of Sale systems
across 23 countries to ensure reliable in-person payment processing and
fiscalization compliance.
 - Oversaw architecture of the multi-platform solution pluginizing 3rd-party
payment and fiscalization systems.
 - Oversaw the foundation for quick product data-driven discovery experiments
 - Responsible for critical-path services (6 backends, over 7 microfrontends),
including its technical projects, such as migration from legacy monolith
 - Focused on team growth, technical debt reduction, and establishing sustainable
delivery processes with clear ownership and incident management

- Founded and led development of a self-service kiosk platform deployed across 18
countries on 2000+ units, integrated with 25 payment providers (8 proprietary)
 - Delivered a unified web-based experience across desktop and mobile, supporting
2M monthly orders and increasing average check by 12%
Grew team size by 100%
 - Aligned technical architecture with product metrics
 - Ensured seamless hardware-software integration for payment, receipt, and
secure mode functionality

- Sustained and evolved a distributed POS system across 15 countries, managing
backend, frontend, and desktop services
 - Drove technical strategy, prioritized backlog, identified technical debt, and led
migration from monolith to domain services
 - Participated in full feature lifecycle, from refinement to operational support, with
emphasis on non-functional requirements and system reliability

- Contributed to a full-stack autonomous team within a larger LESS structure,
implementing features for cashier interfaces, monolith decoupling, new countries
support
 - Participated in monitoring, incident response, postmortems, and reliability
enhancements
 - Facilitated team meetings and contributed to local engineering communities

- Led a cross-regional web team focused on infrastructure and customer-facing
features for the iTero platform
 - Contributed to refactoring legacy components, enhancing logging/monitoring,
and building cloud-native services like desktop notifications for lab assistants
 - Participated in hiring, technical architecture discussions, and internal initiatives

- Migrated monolithic applications to microservices on AWS, enabling regional data synchronization with 3D scanners and lab software\n-  Developed APIs, maintained performance, and integrated with internal data hubs using Siren client\n- Supported hiring and onboarding of new engineers.

- Developed the MyAlignTech platform for 3D dental case tracking, billing, subscription, and scanner management\n - Worked on metadata synchronization, performance optimization under increasing load, and embedded functionality in iTero scanners\n - Collaborated in a distributed Moscow-Tel Aviv team using Scrum and XP methodologies.

- Developed a custom SCORM-based Learning Management System for cabin attendants, pilots, and technicians, featuring interactive courses, webinars, tests, and administrative tools using .NET and Silverlight.\n - Built a system for tracking English test results and scheduling between teachers and airline employees using ASP.NET MVC, jQuery, and SQL Server 2012.
